hints.title: Target Element Sorting
hints.text: Sorting the array makes it optimal to elevate smaller adjacent elements to equal the maximum element in a subarray.

hints.title: Contiguous Window Cost
hints.text: For a contiguous subarray ending at right, the total operations needed to make all elements equal to nums[right] is window_len * nums[right] - sum.

hints.title: Sliding Interval Expansion
hints.text: Expand the right pointer while shrinking the left pointer whenever the required operations exceed budget k.

hints.title: Full Implementation
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def maxFrequency(self, nums: list[int], k: int) -> int:
        nums.sort()
        left = 0
        total = 0
        ans = 1
        for right in range(len(nums)):
            total += nums[right]
            while nums[right] * (right - left + 1) - total > k:
                total -= nums[left]
                left += 1
            ans = max(ans, right - left + 1)
        return ans
```

complexity.whyNaiveFails: Checking all pairs of subarray bounds takes O(n^2) quadratic time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Sorting in O(n log n) enables a sliding window pass that processes all elements in O(n) time.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate formulates the window cost formula and slides bounds monotonically.
